basis.design_case: 802.3af (D-01: first build is af-classified; requirements s3.1 'Design against af')

envelope_w.source: ICD s6.2 TOTAL across all three rails - the per-rail ceilings do not add up and the total is what binds

bank_uf.source: energy-store.md s7, 4 x Ymin LKMJ2502A681MF 680 uF/100 V

string.arrangement: 12x2 Cree XP-G2 at 1.30 A/die, off-board on its own heatsink

basis.invariant: P_board = P_rail * (48 - V_string)/48 + P_housekeeping  (af 2.33 W, at 4.78 W); P_FETs_only = P_rail * (48 - V_string - V_shunt)/48  (af 2.13 W, at 4.67 W). Independent of flash rate, flash energy, bank capacitance and bank voltage.

rails.vin: J3 pins 1/3/5 - carrier eFuse output, dead at power-up for hundreds of ms (ICD s8.3)
rails.topology_detail: no local regulator; a hot-swap / dv-dt-limited constant-current charge path feeds the bank. It is a current limiter, not a voltage converter.
rails.peak_basis: charge-path ILIM setting; refdesign D11 caps it at 0.6 A because the TPS2378 PD limits at 0.85 A MIN with a 500 us MIN foldback deglitch

consumers.name: bank charge path (dv/dt limited)
consumers.source: P_avail/48; ramp rate set so the 0.75 s cold start stays inside the 8.5 W envelope

consumers.name: TPS2490 hot-swap controller VCC
consumers.source: TI SLVS503F s6.5 - 450 uA typ / 1000 uA max, enabled

consumers.name: PROG/VREF setting divider
consumers.source: estimate from TPS2490 VREF 4 V / I_VREF <= 1 mA; confirm at P3

rails.headroom: 175 mA of the 0.25 A af rail ceiling (70%) and of the 5.40 A connector capacity (3.2%). The 8.5 W TOTAL binds, not the rail.

rails.topology_detail: 2720 uF / 100 V energy store, operating 40-48 V. Behind the carrier's 802.3 compliance load switch AND behind this board's charge FET.

consumers.name: LED string (pulse, via the off-board harness)
active bleed 1 k (only when ENABLE is de-asserted; powered by the bank, costs zero budget)

rails.dissipation_note: bank ESR 43.9 mohm at 120 Hz -> 0.114 V IR sag at 2.6 A = 1.43% of the 8 V window; 2.5 mJ per flash

rails.topology_detail: decoupling only, no local regulator. Keep local bulk <= 4.7 uF so the loop dies promptly on unplug.

consumers.name: LM2904 dual op-amp (error amp + setpoint buffer)

rails.decision: The analogue loop is biased from +12V, NOT +3V3 and NOT a local 48 V linear. Controlling constraint: the pass FET source sits 0.52 V above GND on the shunt and a planar (non-logic-level) HEXFET needs 5-7 V of Vgs at 2.6 A; from 3.3 V an amplifier delivers only 2.78 V, below the worst-case Vgs(th) of 4 V. +3V3 would force a logic-level trench part, which refdesign D6-D8 identifies as the worst choice for a linear pass element. ICD s6.3's 'take power on +48V_SW' targets rail-scale loads worth 0.67 W; at 1.28 mA the conversion penalty is 1.7 mW and the board still takes 100% of its actual power on +48V_SW. A local 48 V linear costs 2.7x the budget, adds a 48 V-domain part, and is dead for the hundreds of ms when +48V_SW is dead - exactly when the gate must be actively held low.
rails.headroom: 0.17% of the 0.75 A af ceiling; 976x below the 1.25 A at-ceiling that busts the carrier's converter thermal budget

consumers.name: LM2903 over-temperature comparator (RECOMMEND MOVING TO +12V - see risk)

consumers_on_signal_pins.name: setpoint RC divider 5k36+1k00 (driven from a PWM pin)
ID divider bottom leg (top leg is the carrier's 10 k)

rails.risk: With the loop biased from +12V, the drive stage is FULLY FUNCTIONAL with the daughter's +3V3 absent (ENABLE and PWM arrive at carrier levels, the setpoint divider runs off the PWM pin, the charge path's EN is GND-referenced). The only casualty is the +3V3-powered over-temperature comparator - i.e. the STR-REQ-20 firmware-independent protection. Recommend biasing the OT comparator and its NTC reference from +12V and taking ADC1 telemetry from an independent +3V3 leg.

power_constraints._note: sustained is only 0.175 A; sized to the 0.6 A charge-path ILIM because this stub carries fault current until the limiter acts

2.6 A pulse at 6.7-14.7% duty; RMS 0.71 A (af) / 1.05 A (at) / 1.21 A (opening burst). Thermally RMS binds but the IR-drop target binds harder: keep total pulse-loop copper under 30 mohm (78 mV = 1% of the window)
harness conductor to the string anode. pdn:false - D1/refdesign forbids capacitance across the string (decay tail)
harness return to the pass FET drain. Also the pass FET's thermal pour net. pdn:false by design
pass FET source to shunt high side. Kelvin-sense the shunt (sense traces to the pad ends); analogue return meets the pulse return only at the shunt low side

thermal_constraints._element: linear pass FET (D2PAK on ~645 mm2 of drain copper)
thermal_constraints._basis: af, 25 Hz, bank charged to 48 V: P = P_avail * (V_mean - 0.114 - V_string - V_shunt)/48 = 1.884 W, declared as 1.9 W. Integrated over the flash (Vds falls 12.18 -> 4.18 V), NOT the 31.7 W peak.
thermal_constraints._allowance: D2PAK RthJA 40 C/W on 1 in2 -> 1.73 W at 56 C air / Tj 125 C. 1.90 W is a 10% overrun; regulating the bank to a ~42 V set-point instead of 48 V drops this to 1.06 W (1.63x margin) at identical light output.
thermal_constraints._at_case: 3.54 W at 802.3at 25 Hz vs a 1.40 W allowance at 69 C air - fails 2.5x. See OPEN-1.
thermal_constraints._layout: the pour is the DRAIN, a 48 V-domain net: the 0.60 mm outer clearance applies to its whole perimeter on every layer and through the board. Excluded from the DC-DC hot zone (2,46)-(36,68) and the antenna column (88,25)-(100,55).

thermal_constraints._element: bank charge FET (high-side N-channel, D2PAK; tab = drain = +48V_SW)
thermal_constraints._basis: steady state P = P_avail * (48 - V_mean)/48; 0.22 W (af 25 Hz, charge to 48 V) to 1.06 W (af, 42 V balanced set-point) to 1.53 W (at, full-window). 1.1 W covers the af design envelope.
thermal_constraints._transient: COLD START is the larger event and is easy to miss: 3.133 J, 8.35 W peak decaying to 0 over 0.75 s at a 0.175 A ramp, in linear mode. Lands in the dead zone between the last plotted 10 ms SOA curve and the DC line on every JLC-stocked MOSFET datasheet (protection-sense s0).
thermal_constraints._repeat_rule: mean = 3.133 J x ENABLE cycles/s. At 1.33 s re-arm the mean hits the 2.35 W D2PAK steady limit. FIRMWARE CONTRACT: ENABLE is a slow arm/disarm with a minimum ~10 s re-arm interval (0.31 W mean); it is NOT a per-flash or per-cue gate - PWM is.

thermal_constraints._basis: 3.133 J dumped over a 4.3 s event: 2.30 W peak at t=0, 0.73 W mean. Costs zero rail budget - the carrier's 48 V switch is already open when it runs.
thermal_constraints._recommendation: split into 2 x 470 ohm 2512 in series: halves the per-part peak to 1.15 W (1.7x inside a 2 W continuous rating, so no joule rating is needed - none is published for any JLC-stocked chip resistor) and doubles the working-voltage margin. Costs $0.09.
thermal_constraints._failsafe: MUST be self-powered from the bank and default ON with every rail dead - bias up from /VBANK through a clamped high-value resistor and have the ENABLE-driven device pull it DOWN to disarm. An ENABLE-inverting stage powered from +3V3 cannot invert anything after a cable unplug, which is exactly the case it exists for.

voltages._note: TPS2490 V_GATE-OUT is 12-16 V above VCC (SLVS503F s6.5) - the highest-voltage net on the board. Still inside the IPC-2221B B2 51-100 V band, so the ICD's 0.60 mm covers it. Do NOT declare the TVS clamp voltage (93.6 V) as a working voltage: IPC-2221 spacing is for steady-state working voltage, and 100 V would demand 1.5 mm and fail the layout for no reason.

charge_path_efficiency.formula: eta = V_mean / 48, independent of the charge current profile (E_fet = C * integral(48 - Vc) dVc)
charge_path_efficiency._note: ~92% is high precisely because the 48->40 V window is narrow (44 V mean against a 48 V source). This is what makes a linear charge path acceptable and a switching pre-regulator not worth its parts, area or DC-DC-hot-zone conflict. The cold start pays the classic 50% penalty.

max_full_window_rate_hz._vs_icd: ICD s6.4 quotes 8.6 / 18.8 Hz. Those are the ideal-charge figures (8.5 W / 0.986 J). Adding the 8.33% charge-path loss, 114 mW of housekeeping and the as-built 2720 uF gives 8.0 / 17.6 Hz - 7% lower. Design the governor to 8.0 Hz.

str_req_05_worst_case.scenario: ~30 s of continuous 25 Hz, af, then return to normal
str_req_05_worst_case._note: Duration is NOT the worst case - an indefinite run is, and it is the same 2.35 W, because the rail caps input at 8.5 W however long the drop lasts. 30 s is LESS severe than steady state: the D2PAK+pour time constant is order 60-120 s, so a 30 s burst reaches only 60-80% of the final rise. The bank does not walk down; it sawtooths 45.43 <-> 48.00 V.

burst_from_full_bank_25hz_af._note: Algebra, not a shortfall: one full flash IS the whole 48->40 V window, and 40 ms of rail replaces only 6.99 mC of the 21.76 mC spent. Opening the window to the true 36.7 V regulation floor buys ONE intermediate step: 100% -> 73% -> 32%. At 8 Hz every flash is 100% indefinitely.
burst_from_full_bank_25hz_af._for_the_human: A build-up ending on one maximum blast is supported. A sustained 25 Hz machine-gun section runs at 32% of full energy (0.247 J of LED drive, 2.69 ms wide). Both are musically useful; the second is not blinding.

energy_budget.cold_start_recommendation: Set the RAMP at ~0.175 A via dv/dt (gate-capacitor) control and the CURRENT LIMIT separately at <= 0.6 A as a fault backstop. These are two different numbers. The 0.6 A ILIM protects against PD foldback (TPS2378 ILIM min 0.85 A, deglitch min 500 us). The 0.175 A ramp keeps the whole 750 ms cold start inside the 8.5 W envelope so the PSE overload timer (50-75 ms) is never started - a 0.25 A ramp holds 12 W for 520 ms, seven times the overload window. Do NOT use power-limiting alone as the ramp control: with Vds*Id = PLIM the input current RISES as the cap charges, so input power grows from PLIM to 6*PLIM by 40 V. Program the fault timer longer than 0.75 s or a normal start latches the controller off.

bleed._note: The carrier fits no series diode on +48V_SW, so this board's bleed is not stranded above the carrier's. A board pulled off the stack holds a handling hazard for 7.1 min on the passive path alone - the self-powered active bleed is what makes it 4.3 s in every case with no rail and no firmware.

_d2pak_allowance_w._basis: RthJA 40 C/W on 1 in2 of copper, drive-stage.md s1.2 (datasheet-conditioned). Tj 125 C is a 50 C derate on the 175 C max - standard for a part with no linear-mode SOA characterisation (drive-stage s1.1/R3).

dissipation_map_w._esr_convention: The bank ESR row is carved OUT of the pass FET share, not added to it: the bank's 0.114 V IR sag reduces the terminal voltage the pass FET sees. Each column sums exactly to board_total.
dissipation_map_w._af_columns_identical: af board total is the same at 8.6 and 25 Hz - that is the invariant. Only the split between the two FETs moves.

fet_burden_split._note_esr: pass figures in this table include the 20-44 mW bank-ESR term that dissipation_map_w carves out separately; it changes no conclusion here
fet_burden_split.recommendation_af: Regulate the bank to a ~42 V set-point rather than charging to 48 V. Both FETs then sit at 1.06 W against a 1.73 W allowance (1.63x) instead of one at 1.90 W against 1.73 W (a 10% overrun). Identical average light, identical total heat, half the worst-case junction. Raise the set-point toward 48 V only when burst headroom is wanted - the bank-voltage feedback needed for that is already required by STR-REQ-18.
fet_burden_split.warning: Paralleling two pass FETs is NOT a free fix: linear-mode paralleling is unstable without source ballast (the lower-Vgs(th) device hogs current, heats, and its threshold falls further - the Spirito mechanism of refdesign D6), and source ballast re-introduces the dropout headroom this design is trying to save.

sequencing.no_mate_ordering: ICD s7.3 - a dual-row header has no first-mate/last-mate control. 48 V may arrive before or after 3.3 V, in either order, on mate AND on unmate.

power_up_48v_dead.state: ENABLE low (carrier 10 k + daughter 100 k, both passive); charge path off (TPS2490 GATE held below POR ~6 V / UVLO, and its EN pin is GND-referenced with 100 V abs max so ENABLE drives it with no rail); pass FET off (gate-source pull-down + 2N7002 clamp, both rail-independent); bank at 0 V.
power_up_48v_dead.hard_rule: No component may bridge +12V or +3V3 to +48V_SW, /VBANK, /LED_A or /LED_K (ICD s8.3 point 2). The only nets crossing the domain boundary are ENABLE/PWM into GND-referenced control inputs, and the bank-sense divider tap - a resistive path OUT of the 48 V domain into a high-impedance ADC. Make this an explicit netlist review item at P4 and a check at P8: it is the one requirement whose violation is invisible on the bench and only shows up as a PD compliance failure.
power_up_48v_dead.port_capacitance: Total daughter capacitance on the +48V_SW side of the charge FET must stay under ~1 uF (TVS + controller bypass only) = 0.56% of the 802.3 180 uF ceiling, against the carrier's own 44 uF. The 2720 uF sits BEHIND the charge FET, where the carrier's compliance switch already hides it.

enable_assert_into_empty_bank.sequence: carrier eFuse closes fast into <1 uF (non-event) -> TPS2490 clears POR/UVLO -> GATE released through its dv/dt capacitor -> constant ~0.175 A, 0->48 V in 0.75 s, 3.133 J burnt in the charge FET (8.35 W falling to 0). The carrier's eFuse ILIM (1.0 A) sits ABOVE the daughter's ramp so the two soft-starts do not fight (ICD s8.2).
enable_assert_into_empty_bank.requirement: Inhibit the drive stage until the bank clears the regulation floor. Below ~36 V the string cannot conduct; between 36 and 40 V a commanded flash produces a truncated dim pulse and steals the charge current. Recommend a bank-undervoltage lockout at ~40 V on the FREE second section of the LM2903 (protection-sense s4 notes it is spare). This also removes the 'first flash of a phrase fades in' mode of refdesign E2.
enable_assert_into_empty_bank.worst_mate_order: ENABLE connects before +48V_SW -> the charge path is armed when the rail arrives. Handled by the dv/dt ramp - the event is the same either way. GND-last is not reachable: 2.54 mm dual-row pins mate within ~0.3 mm of travel and there are 12 GND pins with a GND adjacent to every supply pin.

enable_deassert_mid_flash.sequence: 2N7002 clamp pulls the pass gate to source in ~us -> string current stops -> charge path stops -> bank holds charge -> active bleed engages, 48->10 V in 4.3 s.
enable_deassert_mid_flash.harness_clamp_requirement: Harness inductance is the only stored energy needing somewhere to go: 0.5-2 uH at 2.6 A = 1.7-6.8 uJ, producing 13-52 V of L*di/dt at a 100 ns turn-off, on top of a 48 V bank. Clamp the drain with a drain-source TVS or verified avalanche capability - NOT a freewheel diode across the string, which recirculates harness current through the LEDs and produces exactly the decay tail STR-REQ-01 forbids. The energy is trivial; the topology is not.
enable_deassert_mid_flash.re_arm_penalty: minimum ~10 s between ENABLE assertions (see thermal_constraints Q_CHG). Nuance: the active bleed's 2.72 s time constant makes a SHORT de-assert cheap - a 100 ms glitch drops the bank only ~3.5%. The penalty is graduated, not a cliff.

cable_unplug_mid_flash.hazard: All three rails vanish in arbitrary order. The bank still holds up to 3.133 J at 48 V, and the carrier fits NO series diode on +48V_SW (ICD s8.2), so the bank back-feeds onto the connector's 48 V pins.
cable_unplug_mid_flash.charge_fet_does_not_isolate: A high-side N-channel charge FET's body diode points the wrong way to block bank-to-connector current when the FET is off. Assume the connector pins go to bank potential.
cable_unplug_mid_flash.pass_fet: The passive gate-source pull-down turns it off with every rail dead. Keep +12V local bulk <= 4.7 uF so a still-powered op-amp cannot hold the gate up after ENABLE has gone.
cable_unplug_mid_flash.active_bleed: MUST be self-powered from the bank and default ON with every rail dead. An ENABLE-inverting stage powered from +3V3 cannot invert anything after an unplug, which is exactly the case it exists for. Bias it up from /VBANK through a clamped high-value resistor; have the ENABLE-driven device pull it DOWN to disarm. Prefer a MOSFET-gate arrangement (~2-3 mW standing cost when armed) over a base-driven BJT (~58 mW).
cable_unplug_mid_flash.result: With the self-powered active bleed the board is under 10 V 4.3 s after unplug in every case, with no rail and no firmware. Without it, a board pulled off the stack holds a handling hazard for 7.1 minutes. Silkscreen the stored-energy warning and the bleed time constant per requirements s8.3 regardless.

layout_consequences: Pulse-loop nets are declared at 2.6 A; RMS is only 0.71 A (af) / 1.05 A (at) / 1.21 A (opening burst). Thermally RMS binds, but the IR-drop target binds harder: keep total pulse-loop copper under 30 mohm so the drop stays under 78 mV = 1% of the 8 V window. At 1 oz that forces ~1 mm minimum anyway.

Return the pulse loop directly beneath the outbound conductor on the adjacent layer (refdesign L1/L6). Vertical coupling shrinks the loop area without violating the in-plane 0.60 mm 48 V clearance, and inner-layer clearance is JLC's 0.127 mm minimum anyway, so the vertical dimension is free.

Kelvin-sense the shunt with sense traces to the pad ends (no 4-terminal 2512 exists on JLC). Route the sense pair tight, not parallel to the pulse path; the analogue return meets the pulse return only at the shunt low side; the bank-sense divider must reference the same quiet point (refdesign L2).

The pass FET's 645 mm2 drain pour is a 48 V net excluded from the DC-DC hot zone (2,46)-(36,68) and the antenna column (88,25)-(100,55), and carries the 0.60 mm clearance on its whole perimeter on every layer including through-board. If that area cannot be met the RthJA rises and the af margin disappears - check at P5/P6, not at P8 (drive-stage R5).

Connector loading: +48V_SW carries 175 mA sustained / 600 mA peak of a 5.40 A capacity (3.2% / 11%) at the ICD's 1.80 A/pin derate. The 2.6 A pulse NEVER crosses the connector - it comes from the bank.

open.q: D-01 says the 802.3at upgrade is 'a resistor change + a PoE+ switch, no respin'. For this daughter it is not: at 18.386 W the two linear FETs must dissipate 4.67 W between them in 69 C air. Best case (balanced split, 38 V string) is 1.91 W per D2PAK against a 1.40 W allowance - fails 1.4x; the simple case fails 2.6x. Closing it needs RthJA <= 15-24 C/W (a real heatsink on a 48 V-domain drain tab), or a string above 40.2 V (over the ICD's 38 V ceiling, unavailable), or a governor cap of 11.0 W (35.3 V string) / 14.2 W (38 V string) of the 18.5 W available.
open.recommendation: Build to af as requirements s3.1 already directs, and record that the at path costs this daughter either a heatsinked pass element or a governor-imposed ~11-14 W cap. NOT a blocking issue against LUM-CAR-A - the carrier's ICD is correct and nothing this board needs from it changes. The board is not unsafe in at mode (STR-REQ-20's firmware-independent trip is the backstop) - it just does not deliver the extra light the upgrade promises.

open.severity: lever, needs the human because it moves an ICD number
open.q: The ICD's 40 V window floor was set for a 38 V string. With the recommended 12x2 XP-G2 array at 35.3 V the true regulation floor is 36.71 V, leaving 3.3 V and 0.34 J of unused window - a 36% larger accent for zero parts cost. It buys burst energy only: it does NOT raise the sustained rate (rail-bound) and does NOT reduce dissipation (the invariant).
open.recommendation: Take it if the single-blast accent matters. Flagged rather than adopted because it changes a number the ICD states.

open.q: String voltage is the single most sensitive input in the whole thermal design: every extra volt moves P_rail/48 = 2.1% of the budget (af 175 mW) from the pass FET to the LED. 35.3 V -> 38.0 V cuts board dissipation from 2.13 W to 1.75 W (-18%) and adds the same 0.38 W to the light. led-emitter s3 chose 12x2 XP-G2 because 13 in series is 38.2 V and breaks the <=38 V limit - but that limit exists to preserve headroom at a 40 V floor which OPEN-2 shows is itself a consequence, not a constant.
open.recommendation: Re-run the emitter arrangement against a jointly-chosen (string voltage, window floor) pair rather than treating either as fixed. Coupled decision across led-emitter, drive-stage and this block.

open.severity: single-point failure of a firmware-independent protection
open.q: With the loop biased from +12V, the drive stage is fully functional with the daughter's +3V3 absent (ENABLE and PWM arrive at carrier levels, the setpoint divider runs off the PWM pin to GND, the charge path's EN is GND-referenced). The only casualty is the +3V3-powered over-temperature comparator - i.e. STR-REQ-20. The exposed case is a daughter-local loss of +3V3 (both pins open, a broken track, a shorted decoupling cap) while the carrier is healthy; a carrier-side 3.3 V failure is self-safing because ENABLE de-asserts.
open.recommendation: Bias the OT comparator and its NTC reference divider from +12V (LM2903 is 2-36 V; its open-collector output sinks a 12 V gate node fine) and take ADC1 telemetry from an independent +3V3-referenced leg. Two thermistors on the off-board module cost $0.08 and also mean a shorted telemetry wire cannot defeat the trip. Circuit shape is the architect's call; the power-architecture requirement is: the protection must sit on a rail no less available than the thing it protects.

open.q: ENABLE re-arm rate. Mean charge-FET power = 3.133 J x ENABLE cycles/s; at a 1.33 s interval the mean hits the 2.35 W D2PAK steady-state limit at 56 C.
open.recommendation: Write into DOC-01 and the carrier's firmware interface: ENABLE is a slow arm/disarm with a minimum ~10 s re-arm interval (0.31 W mean). It is NOT a per-flash or per-cue gate - PWM is. Also record the governor contract that drive-stage s5.1 derived: amplitude must be programmed at least one flash period (~5 ms) before the flash it applies to.

open.q: Two numbers in the housekeeping budget are estimates, not datasheet reads: the TPS2490 PROG/VREF setting-divider current (~0.100 mA assumed) and the string Vf-vs-current curve used for the reduced-amplitude efficiency estimate (LED share 76% at full amplitude falling to ~68% at 10%).
open.recommendation: Both are second-order (0.1% and a few percent of an already-small term) and neither changes a conclusion. Confirm at P3 when the parts are fixed.
